tagline: A worked EXAMPLE arch.json. Five containers, a self-hosted embedding model and a hosted LLM, behind JWT. Every field this skill supports appears somewhere below.
source_of_truth: example only — in a real run this reads 'docker-compose.yml, api/config.py, api/ai/* @ <commit>'

nodes.name: User's browser
nodes.role: Single-page app; holds the JWT in localStorage.

nodes.name: Web · nginx
nodes.role: Serves the built SPA and reverse-proxies /api to the API.

nodes.name: API · FastAPI
nodes.role: All business logic, auth, and every model call.

nodes.name: Worker · Celery
nodes.role: Runs ingestion and re-indexing off the request path.

kv.Persistence: none — cache only, safe to lose

nodes.name: Embeddings · TEI
nodes.role: Self-hosted embedding server; never leaves the network.

nodes.name: LLM · hosted
nodes.role: Answer synthesis and the grading guardrail. The only outbound AI dependency.

nodes.name: Reranker · TEI
nodes.role: Deployed and healthy, but NOTHING calls it. Retrieval uses raw cosine top-k today.

kv.Status: provisioned, never imported anywhere in api/

chips: candidate for the next retrieval upgrade

lifecycle: Browser loads the SPA from nginx (static build artifact, no SSR).
User signs in; the API issues an HS256 JWT with a 12h expiry (api/auth/jwt.py:14).
Every /api call carries the token; nginx proxies it through untouched.
A question hits POST /api/ask: the API embeds the query, searches Qdrant top-8, and calls the LLM.
The answer is graded by a second LLM call before it is returned; a failing grade sets needs_review.
Document uploads return immediately and are chunked + embedded by the Celery worker off the request path.

storage.name: pgdata
storage.what: All relational data + the audit log

storage.name: qdrant_data
storage.backup: not backed up — rebuildable from pgdata + uploads (~40 min)

seeding.schema_note: There is no create_all anywhere and the Alembic revisions are incremental patches, not table creations — so the schema and the first org + admin come from db-backup.sql.gz. Skipping the restore leaves you with an empty database the app cannot bootstrap out of.

steps.what: Bring the data tier up first
steps.cmd: docker compose up -d db redis qdrant embed

steps.what: Restore the dump — this creates the schema AND the first org/admin
steps.cmd: gunzip -c db-backup.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T db psql -U acme acme
docker compose run --rm api alembic upgrade head

steps.what: Seed reference data (prompt templates, lookup tables)
steps.cmd: docker compose run --rm api python -m app.seed_reference
docker compose up -d api worker web

steps.what: Build the vector index from the restored documents
steps.cmd: docker compose run --rm api python -m app.reindex --all

steps.what: Demo dataset — wipes tenant data first, dev only

seeding.tests: pytest spins an isolated Postgres + an in-memory vector stub via testcontainers (tests/conftest.py:22); no test ever reaches the hosted LLM — the client is monkeypatched.

security: JWT HS256, 12h expiry, secret from JWT_SECRET env (api/auth/jwt.py:14).
CORS is * when DEBUG=1 and the exact origin otherwise (api/main.py:31) — verify DEBUG is unset in production.
Uploads are extension- and magic-byte-checked, capped at 25 MB (api/routes/upload.py:40).
The LLM API key is read from env at process start and never logged (api/ai/client.py:9).
No PII redaction before text is sent to the hosted LLM — see the AI doc, section 'Context & data path'.
scaling: 4 uvicorn workers; the ceiling is the synchronous LLM call in /api/ask (p95 4.2s) — each in-flight question pins a worker.
Qdrant is single-node with no replication; losing the volume costs a ~40 min reindex, not data.
The embedding server is CPU-only and saturates around 12 concurrent chunk batches — the ingest queue is the natural backpressure point.
Redis has no persistence: a restart drops the cache and any queued-but-unstarted ingest jobs.

deploy.what: Follow the seeding runbook above for a from-zero install

ai.summary: Two model surfaces: a retrieval-augmented answering path and a grading guardrail that gates every answer. Embeddings are self-hosted and never leave the network; answer synthesis and grading go to a hosted LLM. There is no fine-tuning, no training on user data, and no agentic tool use in the answering path.

workflows.name: Document ingestion & indexing
workflows.purpose: Turn an uploaded PDF into searchable chunk vectors. Runs on the worker, off the request path — the upload endpoint returns as soon as the file is on disk.

EX.role: pdfplumber, text layer only — no OCR.

kv.Fails_on: scanned PDFs with no text layer

CH.role: Fixed-size token windows with overlap. No semantic boundary detection.

EM.role: Batched calls to the self-hosted TEI server.

VS.role: One point per chunk; payload carries document_id and page.

io.label: Contract
io.Output: N chunk vectors in Qdrant + a row per chunk in Postgres
io.Latency: ~9s for a 40-page PDF (p50), dominated by embedding

failure: No text layer → document marked unreadable; the user sees it in the doc list, no retry (api/tasks/ingest.py:61).
Embedding server down → Celery retries 3× with 30s backoff, then the task dead-letters.
Partial failure leaves earlier chunks indexed — reindexing is idempotent, so re-running is safe.

workflows.name: Question answering (RAG query path)
workflows.purpose: Answer a question from the indexed corpus. Synchronous — the user waits. This is the only path that sends document text to a hosted model.

diagrams.title: One real request, across the tiers
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant B as Browser
  participant A as API
  participant E as Embed (local)
  participant Q as Qdrant
  participant L as LLM (hosted)
  B->>A: POST /api/ask {question}
  A->>E: embed(question)
  E-->>A: 768-d vector
  A->>Q: search top-8
  Q-->>A: 8 chunks + scores
  A->>L: synthesise(system + chunks + question)
  L-->>A: answer + citations
  A->>L: grade(answer, chunks)
  L-->>A: {grounded: true, score: 0.91}
  A-->>B: 200 {answer, citations, score}
  Note over A,L: two LLM round-trips per question — the grade is not optional

QE.role: Same model as ingestion — a mismatch here silently destroys recall.

SR.role: Plain cosine top-k. No hybrid search, no metadata filter beyond tenant.

kv.Score_floor: none — 8 chunks always come back, however weak

AS.role: Concatenates the chunks under a fixed system prompt. Truncates the oldest history first.

kv.Overflow: drop oldest history turns, then drop lowest-scoring chunks

LM.role: One call, temperature 0.2, citations requested in the output schema.

GD.role: Second call: is the answer grounded in the retrieved chunks?

io.label: Contract
io.Failure_mode: 503 when the hosted LLM is unreachable — there is no local fallback model

failure: 429 from the LLM → 3 retries, exponential backoff (api/ai/client.py:60).
Still failing → 503 to the caller. No fallback model is configured, so the answering path has a hard external dependency.
Grade below 0.7 → the answer is stored but not shown; it lands in the review queue.
Retrieval returning weak chunks is not an error — there is no score floor, so an off-topic question still produces 8 chunks and an answer, which the grader is the only thing catching.

workflows.name: Grounding guardrail
workflows.purpose: The single check standing between a hallucinated answer and the user. Runs on every answer, synchronously, before the response is returned.
workflows.trigger: called inline by the ask path (api/ai/grade.py:22)
chips: no human in the loop below 0.7

diagrams.title: Decision
diagrams.code:
flowchart TD IN(["answer + retrieved chunks"]) --> P["Grading prompt
api/prompts/grade.md"] P --> M{{"claude-sonnet-5
temp 0, json schema"}} M --> S{"score ≥ 0.7 ?"} S -->|yes| PASS(["return to user"]) S -->|no| HOLD(["withhold · needs_review"]) HOLD --> RQ[("review_queue
postgres")] M -.->|error or timeout| FAILOPEN(["fail OPEN
answer returned ungraded"]) classDef risk stroke-dasharray:3 4 class FAILOPEN risk

M.role: Structured output: {grounded: bool, score: float, unsupported_claims: []}.

FAILOPEN.role: If the grading call itself errors or times out, the answer is returned ungraded.

kv.Risk: under an LLM outage the guardrail silently disappears while answers keep flowing

failure: Grader times out (8s) → fail open: the answer is returned ungraded and a grade_skipped event is logged (api/ai/grade.py:71).
Malformed JSON from the model → one retry, then fail open as above.

prompts.name: answer_system
prompts.purpose: Sets the answering persona, citation format, and the refusal rule for unsupported questions

prompts.name: answer_user
prompts.purpose: Assembles retrieved chunks + history + the question
prompts.budget: chunks capped at 6k tokens; history dropped oldest-first

prompts.name: grade
prompts.purpose: Scores whether every claim in the answer is supported by the chunks

context.note: The window is nowhere near full — the 8-chunk cap is a retrieval choice, not a context limit. Raising k is cheap in tokens and would mostly cost latency and grading cost.
context.leaves_the_box: Retrieved chunk text, conversation history and the question go to Anthropic. Embeddings never leave the network. There is no PII redaction step — whatever is in the source documents is what gets sent.
context.retention: Anthropic API standard terms; no training on API inputs. The app itself stores every prompt and completion in ai_calls for audit (api/ai/client.py:88) — that table is the real PII exposure and is not currently redacted or expired.

state_of_play.claim: Every answer is graded before the user sees it
Embeddings are computed locally and never leave the network
A reranker is deployed for retrieval quality
state_of_play.evidence: docker-compose.yml:80 — no import of it anywhere under api/

state_of_play.claim: The answering path degrades gracefully when the LLM is down
state_of_play.evidence: no fallback model in api/ai/client.py; /api/ask 503s — this is the observed behaviour, not a documented design

state_of_play.claim: Scanned PDFs are supported via OCR
state_of_play.evidence: no OCR dependency in requirements.txt; api/tasks/ingest.py:61 marks them unreadable
